title: Luxury in numbers
heading: How far off is your gut?
intro: Eight real numbers about luxury: what people pay, how much is really made, and who buys it.
Every figure is real and sourced. Bet on how sure you are, not just on what you think.

outro.heading: Luxury is a careful balance.
paras: Luxury brands sell quality, but also a story about the people who buy them. Some of these numbers show how high the prices go; others show how much bigger the business is than it looks.
Today, think about what makes customers willing to pay a premium.

questions.q: In July 2025 the original Hermès Birkin bag, made for the singer Jane Birkin in 1985, was sold at auction in Paris. For how much?
questions.explain: €8.6 million including fees, about $10 million: the most ever paid for a handbag. The bag began with a sketch Jane Birkin made for Hermès's boss on a flight in the early 1980s.

questions.q: Between 2022 and 2024, how many customers did the luxury goods industry lose worldwide, according to Bain?
questions.explain: About 50 million, from a base of roughly 400 million in 2022, as prices rose faster than many occasional buyers could follow. Sales fell about 2% in 2024, one of the weakest years on record; by 2025 Bain put the base at about 340 million.
questions.source: Bain & Company / Altagamma, Luxury Goods Worldwide Market Study, November 2024 and November 2025

questions.q: Rolex doesn't publish figures. Morgan Stanley estimated how many watches it made in 2023?
questions.explain: About 1.24 million, with sales of roughly CHF 10 billion: more in sales than its next five rivals combined. Waiting lists come from demand, not tiny production.

questions.q: In April 2025 Hermès became the world's most valuable luxury company on the stock market. Which group did it overtake?
questions.explain: LVMH, which owns more than 75 brands; Hermès earns most of its money from one name. LVMH had quietly built a stake of over 20% in Hermès by 2011, and agreed in 2014 to hand it to its own shareholders.
questions.source: Bloomberg, 15 April 2025; LVMH website; The Fashion Law (LVMH–Hermès timeline)

questions.q: By law, where must genuine Harris Tweed be handwoven?
options: In islanders' homes in the Outer Hebrides
In any mill on Harris or Lewis
Anywhere in Scotland, from Hebridean wool
Anywhere, if Scottish wool is used
questions.explain: In the weavers' own homes in the Outer Hebrides, under the Harris Tweed Act 1993; the wool must also be dyed, spun and finished there. Its Orb mark, registered in 1909, is the oldest British certification mark.

questions.q: In 2019 a Patek Philippe Grandmaster Chime, sold at a charity auction in Geneva, became the most expensive wristwatch ever sold. What did it fetch?
questions.explain: CHF 31 million, at the Only Watch charity auction. It was a one-off steel version of a watch Patek makes only a handful of times.
questions.source: Christie's Geneva, Only Watch auction, 9 November 2019

questions.q: How much did the world spend on personal luxury goods (fashion, bags, watches, jewellery and luxury beauty) in 2024?
questions.explain: About €363 billion. Including luxury cars, hotels, food and wine, total luxury spending is far higher, at well over €1 trillion.

questions.q: How many cars did Ferrari ship to customers worldwide in 2024?
questions.explain: 13,752, up just 0.7% on 2023, yet its net profit rose by about a fifth that year. Fewer cars than people expect, and a lot of money per car.
